title: Vale and the Storm Engine — opening cut

interpolation.note: 8 fps to 48 fps before retiming and 24 fps export

selection_reasons: native 288x512 chosen for cpu/bfloat16 with 5 cores (fast tier: no native bf16 or quality=fast)
GPU-tier models (Wan, LTX, CogVideoX) skipped: no CUDA device
Six-step latent consistency keyframes reduce CPU denoising work.

method_explained.i2v: Six-step LCM keyframe, reference conditioning where available, followed by AnimateDiff-Lightning video-to-video.

specs.edit: hard cuts on the generated music beat grid

visual_review.method: Inspected reference, storyboard keyframes and twelve evenly spaced decoded output frames.
observations: Vale's pale hair, dark collar and silhouette are recognizable across the two shots.
The first shot changes eye highlights and the surrounding light. The second changes framing and rain highlights while the running pose stays similar.
Face detail is soft at full export size, the eye color drifts, and the rooftop shot does not show a complete running stride.
visual_review.runtime_note: 469.7 seconds for the resumed animation, edit and export pass. This excludes reference and keyframe generation on the earlier machine and the interrupted attempt.
visual_review.audio_check: AAC output measured -17.1 dB mean volume. Audio playback was unavailable in this review client.

quality.speech_metric_note: error rate compares Whisper text to the script; number formatting (e.g. 'seven forty-two' vs '7:42') and kana/kanji variants inflate it

limitations: Generated at 288x512 and upscaled 3.8x (Lanczos+unsharp) — export resolution is NOT native detail.
2-second clips (16 frames @ 8 fps) are motion-interpolated to 24 fps; fast action can smear.
4-step distilled motion model on CPU: fine details (hands, small accessories) can warp between frames.
Character identity is guided by a reference image (IP-Adapter/keyframes), not locked; faces can drift in action shots.
No GPU: higher-fidelity open models (Wan, LTX-Video, CogVideoX) were not run.

alternatives_considered.why_not: needs a CUDA GPU (8–24 GB+) and a ~22 GB UMT5-XXL text encoder; impractical on 4 vCPU/15 GB RAM
alternatives_considered.needs: GPU runner (e.g. 24 GB) — plug into model_router via diffusers WanPipeline

alternatives_considered.why_not: T5-XXL encoder + GPU memory; minutes per clip only on GPU
12–24 GB VRAM; very slow on CPU
not yet benchmarked here; candidate for next CPU iteration

recommendations: Run on a GPU runner and switch the router to Wan 2.x I2V for native 480p/720p motion.
Increase native resolution to 512x896 when time allows; add RIFE interpolation instead of minterpolate.
Use pose/ControlNet keyframes for complex action; train a small character LoRA for stronger identity.

reproducibility.seeds_and_prompts: story/storyboard.json (per shot: prompt, seed, camera, method)
reproducibility.note: bf16 vs fp32 and CPU vs GPU produce slightly different pixels for identical seeds.
